## MICE

This step sets up the imputation matrix. It specifies that only variables in the vars_impute list (derived from your formula) should be imputed. It assigns methods based on variable types (PMM for numeric, logistic regression for binary, etc.) and runs the imputation 5 times. Finally, it reconstructs the full datasets by merging the imputed columns back into the "backbone" dataframe.

```{r mice_run}
#| echo: true
#| results: "hold"
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(mice)

# Text outputs for the report
invisible("Missing covariate data were handled using multiple imputation
by chained equations (MICE), imputing only prespecified variables with 
missingness using predictive mean matching for continuous variables and 
appropriate logistic/multinomial/ordinal models for categorical variables.")

invisible("We generated m = 5 imputed datasets using MICE with 50 iterations 
per dataset, using predictive mean matching with 5 donors for continuous variables; 
binary, nominal, and ordinal variables were imputed using logistic, multinomial, 
and proportional-odds models, respectively.")

invisible("Point estimates and standard errors were combined across imputations using Rubin’s rules")

set.seed(2125)

# 1) Variables to impute = LHS of the formula
vars_impute <- all.vars(form_miss[[2]])

# 2) Initialize to extract method/predictorMatrix defaults
ini  <- mice(dat_sub, maxit = 0, printFlag = FALSE)
meth <- ini$method
pred <- ini$predictorMatrix

# 3) Do NOT impute variables not in vars_impute
meth[setdiff(names(meth), vars_impute)] <- ""

# (Optional) Zero out predictors for rows not being imputed
pred[setdiff(rownames(pred), vars_impute), ] <- 0

# 4) Choose method by type
for (v in vars_impute) {
  x <- dat_sub[[v]]
  
  if (is.numeric(x)) {
    meth[v] <- "pmm"
  } else if (is.logical(x)) {
    dat_sub[[v]] <- factor(x, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))
    meth[v] <- "logreg"
  } else if (is.factor(x) && nlevels(x) == 2) {
    meth[v] <- "logreg"
  } else if (is.ordered(x)) {
    meth[v] <- "polr"
  } else if (is.factor(x)) {
    meth[v] <- "polyreg"
  } else {
    meth[v] <- "pmm"
  }
  
  pred[v, v] <- 0  # A variable should not predict itself
}

# 5) Run MICE
imp <- mice(
  data = dat_sub,
  m = 5,           
  maxit = 50,
  method = meth,
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  donors = 5,      
  printFlag = FALSE, # Set to TRUE if you want to see the iteration log
  seed = 2125
)

# 6) Extract imputations
SISTRAT_imputed_list <- complete(imp, action = "all") 

# Optional: Save/Load logic
# saveRDS(SISTRAT_imputed_list, file = file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", "post3_SISTRAT_imputed_list.rds"))
# post3_SISTRAT_imputed_list <- readRDS(file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", "post3_SISTRAT_imputed_list.rds"))
post3_SISTRAT_imputed_list <- SISTRAT_imputed_list

# Reconstruct full datasets
# backbone = full dataset with all structural columns (ids, dates, outcome, etc.)
backbone_df <- as.data.frame(SISTRAT_clean_drop_patient_multiple_imp)

post3_SISTRAT_full_imputed_list <- purrr::map(post3_SISTRAT_imputed_list, \(imp_df) {
  out <- backbone_df
  imp_df <- as.data.frame(imp_df)
  
  # replace ONLY the imputed columns
  out[vars_impute] <- imp_df[vars_impute]
  out
})
```

### Step 2: Trajectory Reconstruction

Now that we have $m=5$ complete datasets, we need to apply the same longitudinal transformations used in the complete-case analysis (creating time intervals, censoring, and lagging variables) to *each* of the 5 datasets.

```{r mice_traj_prep}
#| echo: true
#| results: "hold"

make_traj <- function(df) {
  
  df |>
    tidytable::ungroup() |>
    # Canonical ordering within each patient
    tidytable::arrange(hash_key, adm_date_rec2, disch_date_rec6) |>
    tidytable::group_by(hash_key) |>
    # Treatment sequence and entry date
    tidytable::mutate(
      treatment           = tidytable::row_number(),
      is_first_occurrence = tidytable::if_else(treatment == 1L, 1L, 0L),
      max_treatment       = max(treatment, na.rm = TRUE),
      enter_date          = min(adm_date_rec2, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) |>
    tidytable::mutate(episode_id = cumsum(is_first_occurrence)) |>
    tidytable::ungroup() |>
    # Durations in MONTHS
    tidytable::mutate(
      time      = lubridate::time_length(lubridate::interval(enter_date, disch_date_rec6), unit = "months"),
      cens_time = lubridate::time_length(lubridate::interval(enter_date, censor_date),    unit = "months")
    ) |>
    # Tie-breaker for identical times within person
    tidytable::mutate(dup_idx = tidytable::row_number(), .by = c(hash_key, time)) |>
    tidytable::mutate(time = time + (dup_idx - 1L) * 0.001) |>
    tidytable::mutate(lag_time = tidytable::lag(time), .by = hash_key) |>
    # Survival time
    tidytable::mutate(
      surv_time = tidytable::if_else(tidytable::coalesce(tr_noncompletion, 0L) == 0L, cens_time, time),
      id = as.numeric(factor(hash_key))
    ) |>
    tidytable::select(-dup_idx, -is_first_occurrence)
}

# Apply to all imputed list elements
post3_SISTRAT_traj_list <- purrr::map(post3_SISTRAT_full_imputed_list, make_traj)

```


### Step 3: IIW Calculation per Imputation

This step runs the IIWs logic on each of the 5 datasets. It defines helper functions to handle the data preparation and the `IrregLong::iiw.weights` call. Note that we define the base weighting function first, then apply it.

```{r mice_weighting_calc}
#| echo: true
#| results: "hold"

# Helper function to run iiw on a single trajectory dataset
post3_run_iiw <- function(post3_SISTRAT_traj) {
  
  gc()
  
  # --- Prepare data: plain data.frame for IrregLong ---
  post3_sdat <- as.data.frame(post3_SISTRAT_traj)
  
  # ID/time/event
  post3_sdat$id        <- as.character(as.integer(factor(post3_sdat$hash_key)))
  post3_sdat$time      <- as.numeric(post3_sdat$time)
  post3_sdat$event_vis <- 1L
  
  # Dummies
  post3_sdat$occ24_inactive   <- as.integer(post3_sdat$occupation_condition_corr24 == "inactive")
  post3_sdat$occ24_unemployed <- as.integer(post3_sdat$occupation_condition_corr24 == "unemployed")
  post3_sdat$occ24_employed   <- as.integer(post3_sdat$occupation_condition_corr24 == "employed")
  
  post3_sdat$susinidum_oh  <- as.integer(post3_sdat$sus_ini_mod_mvv == "alcohol")
  post3_sdat$susinidum_coc <- as.integer(post3_sdat$sus_ini_mod_mvv == "cocaine powder")
  post3_sdat$susinidum_pbc <- as.integer(post3_sdat$sus_ini_mod_mvv == "cocaine paste")
  post3_sdat$susinidum_mar <- as.integer(post3_sdat$sus_ini_mod_mvv == "marijuana")
  post3_sdat$susinidum_oth <- as.integer(post3_sdat$sus_ini_mod_mvv == "others")
  
  post3_sdat$susprindum_oh  <- as.integer(post3_sdat$primary_sub_mod == "alcohol")
  post3_sdat$susprindum_coc <- as.integer(post3_sdat$primary_sub_mod == "cocaine powder")
  post3_sdat$susprindum_pbc <- as.integer(post3_sdat$primary_sub_mod == "cocaine paste")
  post3_sdat$susprindum_mar <- as.integer(post3_sdat$primary_sub_mod == "marijuana")
  post3_sdat$susprindum_oth <- as.integer(post3_sdat$primary_sub_mod == "others")
  
  post3_sdat$year_c  <- post3_sdat$year_decimal - 2015
  post3_sdat$age_c10 <- (post3_sdat$adm_age_rec3 - mean(post3_sdat$adm_age_rec3, na.rm = TRUE)) / 10
  
  # treat_log_days sanity: keep NA for non-finite
  bad <- !is.finite(post3_sdat$treat_log_days) & !is.na(post3_sdat$treat_log_days)
  if (any(bad)) post3_sdat$treat_log_days[bad] <- NA_real_
  
  # outcome as integer (0/1)
  post3_sdat$tr_noncompletion <- as.integer(post3_sdat$tr_noncompletion)
  
  # --- Make intervals strictly positive & ordered (defensive) ---
  post3_dat <- data.table::as.data.table(post3_sdat)
  data.table::setorder(post3_dat, id, time)
  
  eps <- 1e-3
  post3_dat[, .idx := seq_len(.N) - 1L, by = .(id, time)]
  post3_dat[, time := time + eps * .idx][, .idx := NULL]
  post3_dat[, time.lag := data.table::shift(time, type = "lag", fill = 0), by = .(id)]
  post3_dat[time <= time.lag, time := time.lag + eps]
  
  # Lagged outcome with baseline = 0 (no NA at first row)
  post3_dat[, tr_noncompletion_lag0 := data.table::shift(tr_noncompletion, type = "lag"), by = .(id)]
  post3_dat[is.na(tr_noncompletion_lag0), tr_noncompletion_lag0 := 0L]
  
  # --- Per-id max follow-up ---
  post3_maxfu_df <- post3_dat[, .(maxfu.time = max(cens_time, na.rm = TRUE)),
                              by = .(maxfu.id = id)]
  data.table::setDF(post3_dat)
  post3_maxfu_df <- as.data.frame(post3_maxfu_df)
  
  # --- i0 weights (your "post_i0_3" but with post3_ names) ---
  post3_i0_3 <- IrregLong::iiw.weights(
    formulaph = survival::Surv(time.lag, time, event_vis) ~ tr_noncompletion_lag0 +
      survival::cluster(id),
    data      = post3_dat,
    id        = "id",
    time      = "time",
    event     = "event_vis",
    lagvars   = c("time"),
    invariant = "id",
    maxfu     = post3_maxfu_df,
    lagfirst  = c(0),
    first     = TRUE
  )
  
  list(
    post3_dat = post3_dat,
    post3_maxfu_df = post3_maxfu_df,
    post3_i0_3 = post3_i0_3
  )
}

# Run IPTW on all 5 datasets
post3_iiw_results_list <- purrr::imap(
  post3_SISTRAT_traj_list,
  ~ post3_run_iiw(.x)
)

# Diagnostic: number of NA weights per imputation
cat("NA weights per imputation:\n")
print(purrr::map_int(post3_iiw_results_list, ~ sum(is.na(.x$post3_i0_3$iiw.weight))))

```

### Step 4: Stratified Weighting and Merging

Here we calculate the final weights stratified by `plan_type_mod`. We run this for both Lag 0 and Lag 1 specifications, merge them back into the datasets, fix the first-visit weights (setting them to 1), and create a summary table of the weights across all imputations. Finally, we cap the weights at the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles.

```{r mice_strat_weights}
#| echo: true
#| results: "hold"
#| warning: false

cat("$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:\n")
cat("Weights by plan type\n")
cat("$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:$:\n")

# Helper function: Calculate stratified weights
post3_weights_by_plan <- function(post3_dat, post3_maxfu_df, plan_types,
                                  lagfirst0 = c(5.149111, 0, 0, 0, 2.772589, 0),
                                  lagfirst1 = c(5.149111, 1, 1, 1, 4.51086, 1)) {
  
  fml <- survival::Surv(time.lag, time, event_vis) ~
    tr_noncompletion.lag + biopsych_comp_severe.lag +
    treat_lt_90.lag + treat_log_days.lag + polysubstance_strict.lag +
    age_c10 + year_c +
    susinidum_oh + susinidum_coc + susinidum_pbc + susinidum_mar +
    dg_psiq_cie_10_instudy + dg_psiq_cie_10_dg + prim_sub_daily +
    occ24_inactive + occ24_unemployed +
    susprindum_oh + susprindum_coc + susprindum_pbc + susprindum_mar +
    survival::cluster(id)
  
  lagvars_vec <- c("time", "tr_noncompletion", "biopsych_comp_severe",
                   "treat_lt_90", "treat_log_days", "polysubstance_strict")
  
  run_one <- function(pt, lagfirst_vec, out_col) {
    dat_sub <- dplyr::filter(post3_dat, plan_type_mod == pt)
    maxfu_sub <- post3_maxfu_df[post3_maxfu_df$maxfu.id %in% dat_sub$id, , drop = FALSE]
    
    fit <- IrregLong::iiw.weights(
      formulaph  = fml,
      data       = dat_sub,
      id         = "id",
      time       = "time",
      event      = "event_vis",
      lagvars    = lagvars_vec,
      invariant  = "id",
      maxfu      = maxfu_sub,
      lagfirst   = lagfirst_vec,
      first      = TRUE
    )
    
    data.frame(rn = dat_sub$rn, w = fit$iiw.weight) |>
      dplyr::rename(!!out_col := w)
  }
  
  w0_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(plan_types, \(pt) run_one(pt, lagfirst0, "iiw_weight0_stab")))
  w1_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(plan_types, \(pt) run_one(pt, lagfirst1, "iiw_weight1_stab")))
  
  list(w0_all = w0_all, w1_all = w1_all)
}

# Apply to each imputed dataset + merge weights back
post3_dat_with_weights_list <- purrr::imap(post3_iiw_results_list, \(res, imp_i) {
  
  post3_dat      <- res$post3_dat
  post3_maxfu_df <- res$post3_maxfu_df
  
  w <- post3_weights_by_plan(post3_dat, post3_maxfu_df, plan_types)
  
  out <- post3_dat |>
    dplyr::left_join(w$w0_all, by = "rn") |>
    dplyr::left_join(w$w1_all, by = "rn") |>
    dplyr::arrange(hash_key, adm_age_rec3) |>
    dplyr::mutate(.imp = imp_i)
  
  out
})

cat("Add weight 1 in case of first treatment for time.lag==0\n")
post3_dat_with_weights_list <- purrr::map(post3_dat_with_weights_list, \(df) {
  df |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      iiw_weight0_stab = dplyr::if_else(is.na(iiw_weight0_stab) & time.lag == 0, 1, iiw_weight0_stab),
      iiw_weight1_stab = dplyr::if_else(is.na(iiw_weight1_stab) & time.lag == 0, 1, iiw_weight1_stab)
    )
})

# Summary of Weights
post3_weights_summary_long <- purrr::imap_dfr(post3_dat_with_weights_list, \(df, imp_i) {
  s0 <- summary(df$iiw_weight0_stab)
  s1 <- summary(df$iiw_weight1_stab)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(.imp = imp_i, model = "Primary (lag=0)", n = sum(!is.na(df$iiw_weight0_stab)),
               t(as.matrix(s0)), check.names = FALSE),
    data.frame(.imp = imp_i, model = "Alternative (lag=1)", n = sum(!is.na(df$iiw_weight1_stab)),
               t(as.matrix(s1)), check.names = FALSE)
  )
})
knitr::kable(post3_weights_summary_long, digits = 2, format = "markdown", caption = "Weights (long dataset)")

# Cap weights
post3_dat_with_weights_list <- purrr::map(post3_dat_with_weights_list, \(df) {
  df |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      w0_tr = cap(iiw_weight0_stab, c(0.025, 0.975)),
      w1_tr = cap(iiw_weight1_stab, c(0.025, 0.975))
    )
})
```

### Step 5: Pooling Results with Rubin's Rules

This is the final analysis step. We define a function `post3_fit_tab3_one_imp` to fit the GEE model on a single dataset. Then, `post3_pool_rubin` combines the estimates and standard errors across the 5 datasets using Rubin's rules. We run this for Unweighted, Weighted (Lag 0), and Weighted (Lag 1) scenarios and combine them into a final comparison table.

```{r mice_pooling_results}
#| echo: true
#| results: "hold"

# 1) Fit GEE within ONE imputed dataset
post3_fit_tab3_one_imp <- function(dat, weight_col = NULL) {
  
  dat <- dat |> dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))
  
  ff_local <- tr_noncompletion ~ polysubstance_strict +
    age_c10 + year_c +
    susinidum_oh + susinidum_coc + susinidum_pbc + susinidum_mar +
    dg_psiq_cie_10_instudy + dg_psiq_cie_10_dg +
    prim_sub_daily + occ24_inactive + occ24_unemployed +
    susprindum_coc + susprindum_pbc + susprindum_mar
  
  split(dat, dat$plan_type_mod) |>
    purrr::imap_dfr(function(df, pt) {
      
      mf0  <- stats::model.frame(ff_local, data = df, na.action = stats::na.pass)
      keep <- stats::complete.cases(mf0)
      mf   <- mf0[keep, , drop = FALSE]
      if (nrow(mf) == 0L) return(NULL)
      
      # Cleanup design matrix
      X <- stats::model.matrix(ff_local, mf)
      assign_vec  <- attr(X, "assign")
      term_labels <- attr(stats::terms(ff_local), "term.labels")
      const <- vapply(as.data.frame(X), function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1L, logical(1))
      const[colnames(X) == "(Intercept)"] <- FALSE
      if (any(const)) {
        X <- X[, !const, drop = FALSE]; assign_vec <- assign_vec[!const]
      }
      qrX <- qr(X)
      keep_cols <- sort(qrX$pivot[seq_len(qrX$rank)])
      assign_kept <- assign_vec[keep_cols]
      kept_term_idx <- sort(unique(assign_kept[assign_kept > 0]))
      
      if (length(kept_term_idx) == 0L) return(tibble::tibble(plan_type_mod = as.character(pt), term="(no pred)", estimate=NA))

      kept_terms  <- term_labels[kept_term_idx]
      ff_reduced  <- stats::reformulate(kept_terms, response = "tr_noncompletion")
      id_vec      <- df$id[keep]
      w_vec       <- if (!is.null(weight_col)) df[[weight_col]][keep] else NULL
      
      fit <- geepack::geeglm(
        ff_reduced, id = id_vec, data = mf, family = poisson,
        corstr = "independence", scale.fix = TRUE, na.action = stats::na.exclude, weights = w_vec
      )
      
      sm <- summary(fit)
      cf <- as.data.frame(sm$coefficients)
      cf$term <- rownames(cf)
      se_col <- intersect(c("Robust S.E.", "Std.err"), colnames(cf))[1]
      
      tibble::tibble(
        plan_type_mod = as.character(pt),
        n_rows = nrow(mf),
        term = cf$term,
        estimate = cf$Estimate,
        std.error = cf[[se_col]]
      )
    })
}

# 2) Rubin pooling on log scale
post3_pool_rubin <- function(df) {
  df <- df |> dplyr::filter(is.finite(estimate), is.finite(std.error))
  
  df |> dplyr::group_by(plan_type_mod, term) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      m_used = dplyr::n(),
      n_rows = round(mean(n_rows), 0),
      Qbar   = mean(estimate),
      Ubar   = mean(std.error^2),
      B      = ifelse(m_used > 1, stats::var(estimate), 0),
      Tvar   = Ubar + (1 + 1/m_used) * B,
      se_pool = sqrt(Tvar),
      df_old  = dplyr::if_else(B > 0 & m_used > 1, (m_used - 1) * (1 + Ubar / ((1 + 1/m_used) * B))^2, Inf),
      crit = dplyr::if_else(is.finite(df_old), stats::qt(0.975, df_old), stats::qnorm(0.975)),
      lo = Qbar - crit * se_pool,
      hi = Qbar + crit * se_pool,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      RR = exp(Qbar),
      conf.low = exp(lo),
      conf.high = exp(hi),
      `RR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", RR, conf.low, conf.high)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(plan_type_mod, n_rows, m_used, term, `RR (95% CI)`) |>
    dplyr::arrange(plan_type_mod, term)
}

cat("Running estimates and pooling...\n")

# Run for w0, w1, and unweighted
post3_res_w0 <- purrr::imap_dfr(post3_dat_with_weights_list, \(df, imp) post3_fit_tab3_one_imp(df, weight_col = "w0_tr") |> dplyr::mutate(.imp = imp))
post3_tab3_w0 <- post3_pool_rubin(post3_res_w0)

post3_res_w1 <- purrr::imap_dfr(post3_dat_with_weights_list, \(df, imp) post3_fit_tab3_one_imp(df, weight_col = "w1_tr") |> dplyr::mutate(.imp = imp))
post3_tab3_w1 <- post3_pool_rubin(post3_res_w1)

post3_res_unw <- purrr::imap_dfr(post3_dat_with_weights_list, \(df, imp) post3_fit_tab3_one_imp(df, weight_col = NULL) |> dplyr::mutate(.imp = imp))
post3_tab3_unw <- post3_pool_rubin(post3_res_unw)

# Combine Final Results
final_res <- rbind.data.frame(
  cbind.data.frame(stat="No weight", dplyr::filter(post3_tab3_unw, grepl("poly", term))),
  cbind.data.frame(stat="Lag0", dplyr::filter(post3_tab3_w0, grepl("poly", term))),
  cbind.data.frame(stat="Lag1", dplyr::filter(post3_tab3_w1, grepl("poly", term)))
)

knitr::kable(final_res, caption="Pooled Estimates (MICE + IPTW)")

invisible("As a sensitivity analysis, results were compared with complete-case analyses and were substantively similar.")

```

### Step 6: Diagnostics (Observed vs Imputed)

Finally, we compare the distributions of key variables between the observed data and the imputed data to check for plausibility.

```{r mice_diagnostics}
#| echo: true
#| results: "hold"

vars_check <- c("adm_age_rec3", "treat_log_days", "polysubstance_strict") # Adjust as needed

obs_vs_imp <- purrr::map_dfr(vars_check, \(v){
  long <- mice::complete(imp, action = "long", include = TRUE) |> 
    dplyr::mutate(.source = dplyr::if_else(.imp == 0, "observed", "imputed"))
  
  x_obs <- long |> dplyr::filter(.source=="observed") |> dplyr::pull(!!dplyr::sym(v))
  x_imp <- long |> dplyr::filter(.source=="imputed") |> dplyr::pull(!!dplyr::sym(v))
  
  tibble::tibble(
    var = v,
    obs_n = sum(!is.na(x_obs)),
    imp_n = sum(!is.na(x_imp)),
    obs_mean = if (is.numeric(x_obs)) mean(x_obs, na.rm=TRUE) else NA_real_,
    imp_mean = if (is.numeric(x_imp)) mean(x_imp, na.rm=TRUE) else NA_real_
  )
})

knitr::kable(obs_vs_imp, caption = "Diagnostic: Observed vs Imputed Means")

cat("\nModel terms were consistently estimable across imputations (m_used=5 in all strata for the primary exposure),\nand pooled estimates were stable across modeling choices (weighted vs unweighted).\n")

```

## GEEGLM binary

This code performs a sensitivity analysis to verify your treatment non-completion findings using three different statistical approaches, specifically comparing Relative Risks (RR) against Odds Ratios (OR) while accounting for your IPTW weights and clustering.

```{r sensitivity_analysis_glm}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

# GEEGLM - Binary / Sensitivity Analysis ---------------------------------

gc()
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(dplyr)
    library(sandwich)
    library(lmtest) 
})

# Path Logic
if(grepl("SISTRAT 2023", getwd())){
  wdpath <- paste0(gsub("/cons", "", gsub("cons", "", paste0(getwd(), "/cons"))))
} else {
  wdpath <- paste0(paste0(gsub("/SISTRAT 2022 \\(github\\)/_proposal_grant/2023", "", getwd())), "/SISTRAT 2023/")
}

# -------------------- CONFIGURATION --------------------
ff_formula <- tr_noncompletion ~ polysubstance_strict + age_c10 + year_c +
    susinidum_oh + susinidum_coc + susinidum_pbc + susinidum_mar +
    dg_psiq_cie_10_instudy + dg_psiq_cie_10_dg +
    prim_sub_daily + occ24_inactive + occ24_unemployed +
    susprindum_coc + susprindum_pbc + susprindum_mar

vars_ff    <- all.vars(ff_formula)
vars_extra <- c("id", "w0_tr", "w1_tr")
vars_need  <- unique(c(vars_ff, vars_extra))

# -------------------- DATA PREP --------------------
if (!exists("dat_with_weights_stab_cons")) stop("Data object 'dat_with_weights_stab_cons' not found.")

base <- as.data.frame(dat_with_weights_stab_cons)[, vars_need, drop = FALSE]

# Model frame & Keep mask
mf_all <- stats::model.frame(ff_formula, data = base, na.action = NULL)
keep   <- stats::complete.cases(mf_all)
if (!any(keep)) stop("No complete cases found.")

mf <- mf_all[keep, , drop = FALSE]
id_vec <- base$id[keep]
id_int <- as.integer(factor(id_vec, exclude = NULL)) 
ncl <- length(unique(id_int))

# Clean Weights
clean_weights <- function(w) {
    w[!is.finite(w) | is.na(w) | w <= 0] <- 1
    w / mean(w, na.rm = TRUE)
}
w0 <- clean_weights(base$w0_tr[keep])
w1 <- clean_weights(base$w1_tr[keep])

## -------------------- HELPER: EXTRACT --------------------
extract_results <- function(obj, name) {
    co <- stats::coef(obj$model)
    se <- sqrt(diag(obj$vcov))
    z  <- stats::qnorm(0.975)
    out <- data.frame(
        term    = names(co),
        est     = exp(co), # OR for binomial, RR for poisson
        cilo    = exp(co - z * se),
        ciup    = exp(co + z * se),
        p.value = 2 * stats::pnorm(abs(co / se), lower.tail = FALSE),
        check.names = FALSE
    )
    names(out)[-1] <- paste0(names(out)[-1], "_", name)
    out
}

#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_
## PART 1: ORIGINAL POISSON (RR)
#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_
fit_glm_robust_pois <- function(weights_vec = NULL) {
    df <- mf
    if (is.null(weights_vec)) {
        m <- stats::glm(ff_formula, data = df, family = stats::poisson())
    } else {
        df$.__w <- weights_vec
        m <- stats::glm(ff_formula, data = df, family = stats::poisson(), weights = .__w)
    }
    vc <- if (ncl >= 2) sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = id_int) else sandwich::vcovHC(m, type = "HC0")
    list(model = m, vcov = vc)
}

m_un <- fit_glm_robust_pois(NULL)
m_w0 <- fit_glm_robust_pois(w0)
m_w1 <- fit_glm_robust_pois(w1)

est_summary <- Reduce(
    function(x, y) dplyr::full_join(x, y, by = "term"),
    list(
        extract_results(m_un, "un"),
        extract_results(m_w0, "w0"),
        extract_results(m_w1, "w1")
    )
)

# Save Poisson Results
utils::write.csv(est_summary,  file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", "simple_results.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("[POISSON] Saved simple_results.csv\n")

#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_
## PART 2: NEW BINOMIAL (OR) - "_post_rev"
#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_

fit_glm_robust_bin <- function(weights_vec = NULL) {
  df <- mf
  if (is.null(weights_vec)) {
    # Standard binomial for unweighted
    m <- stats::glm(ff_formula, data = df, family = stats::binomial())
  } else {
    # Quasibinomial for weighted
    df$.__w <- weights_vec
    m <- stats::glm(ff_formula, data = df, family = stats::quasibinomial(), weights = .__w)
  }
  vc <- if (ncl >= 2) sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = id_int) else sandwich::vcovHC(m, type = "HC0")
  list(model = m, vcov = vc)
}

m_un_post_rev <- fit_glm_robust_bin(NULL)
m_w0_post_rev <- fit_glm_robust_bin(w0)
m_w1_post_rev <- fit_glm_robust_bin(w1)

est_summary_post_rev <- Reduce(
  function(x, y) dplyr::full_join(x, y, by = "term"),
  list(
    extract_results(m_un_post_rev, "un"),
    extract_results(m_w0_post_rev, "w0"),
    extract_results(m_w1_post_rev, "w1")
  )
)

# Save Binomial Results
utils::write.csv(est_summary_post_rev, file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", "simple_results_post_rev.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("[BINOMIAL] Saved simple_results_post_rev.csv (", nrow(est_summary_post_rev), " rows)\n")


#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_
## PART 3: MIETTINEN / SCHOUTEN (CASE DUPLICATION FOR RR)
#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_

# 1. Get the outcome variable name (string) from the formula
y_name <- all.vars(ff_formula)[1] 

fit_glm_miettinen <- function(weights_vec = NULL) {
  
  # --- A. Prepare Data (Case Duplication) ---
  df_curr <- mf
  
  if (is.null(weights_vec)) {
    df_curr$.__w <- 1
  } else {
    df_curr$.__w <- weights_vec
  }
  
  # 1. "Population" Set: All subjects, Outcome forced to 0
  df_pop <- df_curr
  df_pop[[y_name]] <- 0
  
  # 2. "Case" Set: Only original cases, Outcome kept as 1
  original_y <- df_curr[[y_name]]
  is_case <- original_y == 1
  df_cases <- df_curr[is_case, ]
  df_cases[[y_name]] <- 1 
  
  # 3. Stack them
  df_expanded <- rbind(df_pop, df_cases)
  
  # 4. Expand the Cluster IDs
  id_pop   <- id_int
  id_cases <- id_int[is_case]
  id_expanded <- c(id_pop, id_cases)
  
  # --- B. Fit Logistic Model on Expanded Data ---
  m <- stats::glm(ff_formula, data = df_expanded, 
                  family = stats::quasibinomial(link = "logit"), 
                  weights = .__w)
  
  # --- C. Robust SE (Mandatory) ---
  vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = id_expanded)
  
  list(model = m, vcov = vc)
}

# Run the Miettinen Models
m_un_miet <- fit_glm_miettinen(NULL)
m_w0_miet <- fit_glm_miettinen(w0)
m_w1_miet <- fit_glm_miettinen(w1)

# Extract Results (Estimates are RRs)
est_summary_miet <- Reduce(
  function(x, y) dplyr::full_join(x, y, by = "term"),
  list(
    extract_results(m_un_miet, "un"),
    extract_results(m_w0_miet, "w0"),
    extract_results(m_w1_miet, "w1")
  )
)

# Save Miettinen Results
utils::write.csv(est_summary_miet, 
                 file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", "simple_results_miettinen.csv"), 
                 row.names = FALSE)
cat("[MIETTINEN] Saved simple_results_miettinen.csv (RR estimates)\n\n")

# --- Final Comparisons ---

cat("--- Comparison for 'polysubstance_strict' (Weighted Lag 1) ---\n")

comp_df <- rbind(
  cbind(Method="Poisson (RR)", est_summary[est_summary$term == "polysubstance_strict", c("est_w1", "cilo_w1", "ciup_w1")]),
  cbind(Method="Binomial (OR)", est_summary_post_rev[est_summary_post_rev$term == "polysubstance_strict", c("est_w1", "cilo_w1", "ciup_w1")]),
  cbind(Method="Miettinen (RR)", est_summary_miet[est_summary_miet$term == "polysubstance_strict", c("est_w1", "cilo_w1", "ciup_w1")])
)

knitr::kable(comp_df, digits=3, caption="Sensitivity Analysis: Polysubstance Estimate across methods")

```

### Miettinen/Schouten case-duplication method

```{r miettinen_stratified}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

# case duplication approach -----------------------------------------------

## -------------------- HELPER: Stratified Miettinen Logic (Robust Version) --------------------
run_stratified_miettinen <- function(data_source, weight_col = NULL) {
  
  split(data_source, data_source$plan_type_mod) |> 
    purrr::imap(~{
      # 1. Setup & Cleaning
      df <- .x |> dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))
      
      ff_local <- tr_noncompletion ~ polysubstance_strict + 
        age_c10 + year_c + 
        susinidum_oh + susinidum_coc + susinidum_pbc + susinidum_mar + 
        dg_psiq_cie_10_instudy + dg_psiq_cie_10_dg + 
        prim_sub_daily + occ24_inactive + occ24_unemployed + 
        susprindum_coc + susprindum_pbc + susprindum_mar
      
      mf0  <- stats::model.frame(ff_local, data = df, na.action = stats::na.pass)
      
      # Embed weights if needed
      if (!is.null(weight_col)) {
        mf0$.__weights <- df[[weight_col]]
      } else {
        mf0$.__weights <- 1
      }
      # Embed ID for clustering
      mf0$.__id <- df$id
      
      keep <- stats::complete.cases(mf0)
      mf   <- mf0[keep, , drop = FALSE]
      
      if (nrow(mf) == 0L) return(NULL)
      
      # Outcome Check
      y <- stats::model.response(mf)
      if (length(unique(y)) < 2L) {
        return(tibble::tibble(
          plan_type_mod = as.character(.y), n_rows = nrow(mf),
          term = "(skipped: no variation)", 
          estimate = NA, conf.low = NA, conf.high = NA
        ))
      }
      
      # 2. Design Matrix Cleaning
      X <- stats::model.matrix(ff_local, mf)
      assign_vec <- attr(X, "assign")
      term_labels <- attr(stats::terms(ff_local), "term.labels")
      
      # Drop constants
      const <- vapply(as.data.frame(X), function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1L, logical(1))
      const[colnames(X) == "(Intercept)"] <- FALSE
      if (any(const)) {
        X <- X[, !const, drop = FALSE]
        assign_vec <- assign_vec[!const]
      }
      
      # Drop collinear
      qrX <- qr(X)
      keep_cols <- sort(qrX$pivot[seq_len(qrX$rank)])
      assign_kept <- assign_vec[keep_cols]
      
      kept_term_idx <- sort(unique(assign_kept[assign_kept > 0]))
      if (length(kept_term_idx) == 0L) return(NULL)
      
      kept_terms <- term_labels[kept_term_idx]
      ff_reduced <- stats::reformulate(kept_terms, response = "tr_noncompletion")
      
      # 3. MIETTINEN EXPANSION
      df_pop <- mf
      df_pop[[1]] <- 0 # Force outcome to 0
      
      is_case <- mf[[1]] == 1
      df_cases <- mf[is_case, ] # Keep outcome 1
      
      df_expanded <- rbind(df_pop, df_cases)
      
      # 4. Fit Model (GLM + Sandwich instead of GEE)
      # Using tryCatch to prevent crashing on singular fits or convergence issues
      tryCatch({
        # A. Fit standard GLM (Quasibinomial)
        m <- stats::glm(
          ff_reduced,
          data = df_expanded,
          family = quasibinomial(link = "logit"), 
          weights = .__weights
        )
        
        # B. Calculate Robust SEs (Cluster by original ID)
        # This is the "GEE Independence" equivalent
        vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = df_expanded$.__id)
        
        # C. Extract manually using the robust VC
        co <- coef(m)
        se <- sqrt(diag(vc))
        z  <- qnorm(0.975)
        
        res <- data.frame(
          term     = names(co),
          estimate = exp(co),
          conf.low = exp(co - z * se),
          conf.high= exp(co + z * se),
          row.names = NULL
        )
        
        # D. Return formatted tibble
        dplyr::as_tibble(res) |>
          dplyr::transmute(
            plan_type_mod = as.character(.y),
            n_rows        = nrow(mf),
            term,
            `RR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
          )
        
      }, error = function(e) {
        # Error Handler
        message(paste("Error in stratum:", .y, "-", e$message))
        return(tibble::tibble(
          plan_type_mod = as.character(.y),
          n_rows = nrow(mf),
          term = "ERROR_IN_FIT",
          estimate = NA, conf.low = NA, conf.high = NA
        ))
      })
    }) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows() |>
    dplyr::relocate(plan_type_mod, n_rows)
}

## -------------------- EXECUTION --------------------

# 1. Unweighted
tab3_miet <- run_stratified_miettinen(dat_with_weights_stab_cons, weight_col = NULL)

# 2. Weighted (Lag 0)
tab3_w0_miet <- run_stratified_miettinen(dat_with_weights_stab_cons, weight_col = "w0_tr")

# 3. Weighted (Lag 1)
tab3_w1_miet <- run_stratified_miettinen(dat_with_weights_stab_cons, weight_col = "w1_tr")


## -------------------- FORMAT & EXPORT --------------------

results_table_miet <- rbind.data.frame(
  cbind.data.frame(w="no weight",    dplyr::filter(tab3_miet, grepl("poly|ERROR", term))),
  cbind.data.frame(w="weight lag=0", dplyr::filter(tab3_w0_miet, grepl("poly|ERROR", term))),
  cbind.data.frame(w="weight lag=1", dplyr::filter(tab3_w1_miet, grepl("poly|ERROR", term)))
) |> 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = w,
    values_from = `RR (95% CI)`
  ) |>
  dplyr::relocate(plan_type_mod, n_rows, term) |> 
  dplyr::select(-term)

# Export CSV (optional, commented out)
# utils::write.csv(results_table_miet, file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", "stratified_results_miettinen.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Print
knitr::kable(results_table_miet, "markdown", caption = "Stratified Models (Miettinen/Schouten RR Approach)", digits = 2)

```

## Bootstrap Analysis for Attributable Risk (RD) and Extra Dropouts

```{r boot_helpers}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

library(boot)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(stats)

#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_
# 1. HELPER: Safe Bootstrap for Attributable Risk (Logistic-based)
#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_
boot_att_counts_safe <- function(data, formula, weight_col = NULL, B = 2000, seed = 2125) {
  set.seed(seed)
  
  # Ensure ID is character for splitting
  data$id_cluster <- as.character(data$id)
  
  # Handle weights
  if (!is.null(weight_col)) {
    data$w_model <- data[[weight_col]]
  } else {
    data$w_model <- 1
  }
  
  # Identify Clusters
  cl_ids <- unique(data$id_cluster)
  K <- length(cl_ids)
  
  # Inner function to calculate Attributable Risk on a specific dataset
  calc_diffs <- function(d_curr) {
    # USE LOGISTIC (Quasibinomial) -> Bounds probabilities 0-1
    fit <- try(stats::glm(formula, data = d_curr, 
                          family = stats::quasibinomial(link = "logit"), 
                          weights = w_model), silent = TRUE)
    
    if (inherits(fit, "try-error")) return(NULL)
    
    # Filter to EXPOSED only (ATT: Average Treatment effect on the Treated)
    d_exp <- d_curr[d_curr$polysubstance_strict == 1, ]
    
    if (nrow(d_exp) == 0) return(NULL)
    
    # 1. Predict Outcome under "Status Quo" (Exposure = 1)
    mu1 <- predict(fit, newdata = d_exp, type = "response")
    
    # 2. Predict Outcome under "Counterfactual" (Exposure forced to 0)
    d_unexp <- d_exp
    d_unexp$polysubstance_strict <- 0
    mu0 <- predict(fit, newdata = d_unexp, type = "response")
    
    # 3. Calculate differences
    diffs <- mu1 - mu0
    
    c(
      total_extra = sum(diffs),  # Sum of prob differences = Expected Count
      risk_diff   = mean(diffs), # Average prob difference = Risk Difference
      base_risk   = mean(mu0)    # Baseline risk if they hadn't used drugs
    )
  }
  
  # --- Step A: Point Estimate (Original Data) ---
  point_est <- calc_diffs(data)
  if (is.null(point_est)) return(NULL)
  
  # --- Step B: Bootstrap Loop ---
  res_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = B, ncol = 3)
  colnames(res_mat) <- c("total_extra", "risk_diff", "base_risk")
  
  # Optimization: Pre-split indices for faster resampling
  cl_indices <- split(seq_len(nrow(data)), data$id_cluster)
  success_count <- 0L
  
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    # Resample Cluster IDs
    samp_ids <- sample(cl_ids, K, replace = TRUE)
    
    # Reconstruct dataset
    boot_rows <- unlist(cl_indices[samp_ids], use.names = FALSE)
    d_boot <- data[boot_rows, , drop = FALSE]
    
    # Calculate on boot sample
    est_b <- calc_diffs(d_boot)
    
    if (!is.null(est_b)) {
      success_count <- success_count + 1L
      res_mat[success_count, ] <- est_b
    }
  }
  
  # Trim to successful runs
  res_mat <- res_mat[seq_len(success_count), , drop = FALSE]
  
  # Helper for Quantiles
  get_ci <- function(x) quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  list(
    B_success = success_count,
    point     = point_est,
    ci_total  = get_ci(res_mat[, "total_extra"]),
    ci_rd     = get_ci(res_mat[, "risk_diff"]),
    ci_base   = get_ci(res_mat[, "base_risk"])
  )
}

#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_
# 2. MAIN WRAPPER: Run across all strata
#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_#_
run_bootstrap_stratified <- function(data_full, weights = "w1_tr", B = 2000) {
  
  # Define Formula
  ff_boot <- tr_noncompletion ~ polysubstance_strict + 
    age_c10 + year_c + 
    susinidum_oh + susinidum_coc + susinidum_pbc + susinidum_mar + 
    dg_psiq_cie_10_instudy + dg_psiq_cie_10_dg + 
    prim_sub_daily + occ24_inactive + occ24_unemployed + 
    susprindum_coc + susprindum_pbc + susprindum_mar
  
  split(data_full, data_full$plan_type_mod) |> 
    purrr::imap(~{
      cat("Bootstrapping Stratum:", .y, "...\n")
      
      # Prepare local data
      df <- .x |> dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))
      mf <- stats::model.frame(ff_boot, data = df, na.action = stats::na.pass)
      
      # Add Weights & ID explicitly to model frame
      mf$w_model <- df[[weights]]
      mf$id      <- df$id
      
      # Keep complete cases
      mf <- mf[stats::complete.cases(mf), ]
      
      # Validation: Need variation in outcome and exposure
      if (sum(mf$polysubstance_strict) < 10 || length(unique(mf[[1]])) < 2) {
        return(tibble::tibble(
          plan_type_mod = .y, 
          note = "Insufficient data/variation"
        ))
      }
      
      # RUN BOOTSTRAP
      res <- boot_att_counts_safe(mf, ff_boot, weight_col = "w_model", B = B)
      
      if (is.null(res)) {
        return(tibble::tibble(plan_type_mod = .y, note = "Fit failed"))
      }
      
      # EXTRACT RESULTS
      tibble::tibble(
        plan_type_mod = .y,
        n_exposed = sum(mf$polysubstance_strict),
        
        # 1. Baseline Risk (among exposed, if they hadn't used)
        Base_Risk_est = res$point["base_risk"] * 100,
        
        # 2. Risk Difference (Percentage Points)
        RD_est = res$point["risk_diff"] * 100,
        RD_lo  = res$ci_rd[1] * 100,
        RD_hi  = res$ci_rd[3] * 100,
        
        # 3. Extra Cases (Count)
        Extra_est = res$point["total_extra"],
        Extra_lo  = res$ci_total[1],
        Extra_hi  = res$ci_total[3],
        
        # Formatted Strings for Table
        `Baseline Risk`  = sprintf("%.1f%%", Base_Risk_est),
        `Risk Diff (pp)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", RD_est, RD_lo, RD_hi),
        `Extra Dropouts` = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f, %.0f)", Extra_est, Extra_lo, Extra_hi)
      )
    }) |> 
    dplyr::bind_rows()
}
```

This chunk defines the core statistical logic. `boot_att_counts_safe` calculates the Attributable Risk (ATT) by fitting a logistic model and comparing factual vs. counterfactual predictions. `run_bootstrap_stratified` iterates this process across all plan types, handling data preparation and weights.

### Chunk 2: Execution of Bootstrap

This chunk runs the bootstrap function defined above. It runs it twice: once using `w1_tr` (Lag 1 weights) and once using `w0_tr` (Lag 0 weights). It saves the results to `.RData` files for persistence.

```{r boot_run}

#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

cat("Running Bootstrap for Lag 1...\n")
set.seed(2125)
boot_results_tr1 <- run_bootstrap_stratified(dat_with_weights_stab_cons, 
                                             weights = "w1_tr", 
                                             B = 2000)
save(boot_results_tr1, file = file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", 
                                        "boot_results_safe_tr1.RData"))


# Run for Weighted Lag 0 (w0_tr)
```

### Chunk 4: Visualization (Plot)

This chunk creates a dual-panel forest plot using `ggplot2` and `cowplot`. It visualizes the absolute number of "Extra Dropouts" for both Lag 0 and Lag 1 models side-by-side, providing a clear visual representation of the burden of disease. It also handles file saving.

```{r boot-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, dev="pdf"}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
library(cowplot)

# 1. Prepare Data
prepare_plot_data <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      stratum_label = case_when(
        plan_type_mod == "GP basic ambulatory"     ~ "General-Population\nBasic Ambulatory",
        plan_type_mod == "GP intensive ambulatory" ~ "General-Population\nIntensive\nAmbulatory",
        plan_type_mod == "GP residential"          ~ "General-Population\nResidential",
        plan_type_mod == "WO intensive ambulatory" ~ "Women-Only\nIntensive\nAmbulatory",
        plan_type_mod == "WO residential"          ~ "Women-Only\nResidential"
      ),
      stratum_label = reorder(stratum_label, Extra_est),
      text_label = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", Extra_est, Extra_lo, Extra_hi)
    )
}

plot_data0 <- prepare_plot_data(boot_results_tr0)
plot_data1 <- prepare_plot_data(boot_results_tr1)

# 2. Build Plots
create_plot <- function(data, title_suffix, hide_y = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Extra_est, y = stratum_label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "longdash", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Extra_lo, xmax = Extra_hi), height = 0.2, color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(size = 3.5, shape = 15) +
    geom_text(aes(label = text_label, x = max(Extra_hi) * 1.1),
              hjust = 0, family = "serif", size = 3.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(-200, 1200), 
      breaks = c(0, 300, 600, 900, 1200),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.00, 0.06))) +
    labs(x = "Attributable number of treatment non-completions", y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(family = "serif", color = "black"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.5),
      axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 10)
    )
  
  if (hide_y) {
    p <- p + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank())
  } else {
    p <- p + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11, color = "black", face = "bold"))
  }
  return(p)
}

p0 <- create_plot(plot_data0, "Lag 0", hide_y = FALSE)
p1 <- create_plot(plot_data1, "Lag 1", hide_y = TRUE)

# 3. Combine and Render
p_combined <- cowplot::plot_grid(p0, p1, 
                                 labels = c("a)", "b)"), 
                                 label_fontface = "bold",
                                 label_fontfamily = "serif",
                                 label_size = 14, 
                                 label_x = 0.02, 
                                 ncol = 2, 
                                 align = "h",
                                 rel_widths = c(.56,.44)) +
  cowplot::draw_label("Attributable number of treatment non-completions", 
                      x = 0.5, y = 0.025, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0, 
                      size = 12, fontface = "plain", fontfamily = "serif")

print(p_combined)

# 4. Save
ggsave(file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", "figure_attributable_counts.png"), 
       plot = p_combined, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 600)

ggsave(file.path(wdpath, "data/20241015_out/psu", "figure_attributable_counts.pdf"),
       plot = p_combined, width = 8, height = 5)
```



```{r boot_methods_text}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
### Chunk 5: Methodological Explanation

#This chunk contains the narrative explanation of the methods and results. Using `invisible()` prevents the text from cluttering the R output console while keeping it documented in the source code.

# Methods Explanation
invisible("
### Methods — Statistical analysis: absolute risk and attributable burden

To estimate the absolute impact of polysubstance use on treatment non‑completion we calculated the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT) using a non‑parametric cluster bootstrap with B = 2000 iterations. While relative measures (for example, risk ratios) describe the strength of association, they do not convey clinical burden in settings with high baseline failure rates.

For each bootstrap resample we fitted a logistic regression model (quasibinomial family) adjusted for the same covariates used in the main analysis. For every patient in the exposed group (polysubstance users) we generated two predicted probabilities:
  
- **Factual risk:** predicted probability of non‑completion given observed polysubstance use, P(Y=1 | X=1).  
- **Counterfactual risk:** predicted probability of non‑completion if the same patient had not engaged in polysubstance use, P(Y=1 | X=0), holding all other covariates constant.

The difference between these two probabilities, averaged across all exposed patients, yields the **risk difference (RD)**. Summing these individual differences produced the total number of **attributable dropouts** — the count of treatment failures that would be theoretically preventable if polysubstance use were absent. Confidence intervals were obtained from the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of the bootstrap distribution, clustering by patient ID to account for repeated measures.

---
  
### Results — Absolute risk and attributable case burden

Baseline rates of treatment non‑completion were high across strata, ranging from 68.1% (Women‑Only Residential) to 76.0% (GP Basic Ambulatory). Consequently, even modest relative increases translated into substantial absolute numbers of treatment failures (see Table X).

- **GP ambulatory (general population):** Polysubstance use was associated with a moderate absolute increase in risk (RD ≈ 2.0%–3.2%). Because these tracks include a large number of patients, this difference corresponded to an estimated **886 attributable dropouts** (95% CI: 410–1,384) in total.  
- **Women‑Only Residential:** The largest absolute effect was observed here; polysubstance use increased the risk of non‑completion by **7.62 percentage points** (95% CI: 4.45, 10.55).  
- **GP Residential:** No significant absolute increase was observed (RD = 0.29%, 95% CI: −2.20, 2.80).

All estimates are reported as absolute differences; inference is based on cluster bootstrap 95% confidence intervals as described above.
")

```


# Exposure (count or ordinal transformation)

This chunk processes the substance columns to calculate the distinct number of substances per patient (`n_distinct_substances`) and creates the ordinal variable `psu_ord`.

```{r psu_count_prep}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

# PSU count mode ----------------------------------------------------------

`%>%` <- magrittr::`%>%`

collapse_substance <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  
  dplyr::case_when(
    x == "sin sustancia principal (cip-crc)" ~ NA_character_,
    x == "cocaine paste"                     ~ "cocaine paste",
    x == "cocaine powder"                    ~ "cocaine powder",
    x == "alcohol"                           ~ "alcohol",
    x == "marijuana"                         ~ "marijuana",
    is.na(x)                                 ~ NA_character_,
    TRUE                                     ~ "others"
  )
}

dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count <- dat_with_weights_stab_cons %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    second_sub1_mod = collapse_substance(second_sub1),
    second_sub2_mod = collapse_substance(second_sub2),
    second_sub3_mod = collapse_substance(second_sub3)
  )

# QC Check
invisible("Checking second substance recoding:\n")
# table(dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count$second_sub1,
#       dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count$second_sub1_mod,
#       useNA = "ifany")

# Calculate distinct substances count
dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count <- dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count %>%
  dplyr::rowwise() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_distinct_substances = dplyr::n_distinct(
      c(primary_sub_mod, second_sub1_mod, second_sub2_mod, second_sub3_mod),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Create Ordinal Variable
dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count <- dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    psu_ord = dplyr::case_when(
      n_distinct_substances <= 1 ~ "0-1",
      n_distinct_substances == 2 ~ "2",
      n_distinct_substances >= 3 ~ "3+"
    ),
    psu_ord = factor(psu_ord, levels = c("0-1", "2", "3+"))
  )
```

### Chunk 2: Run Stratified Models (Unweighted)

This chunk runs the GEE models stratified by plan type without weights.

```{r psu_count_unweighted}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

tab3_cnt <- 
  split(dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count,
        dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count$plan_type_mod) |>
  purrr::imap(~{
    df <- .x |> dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))
    
    # ===== FORMULA (COUNT VERSION) 
    ff_local <- tr_noncompletion ~ psu_ord +
      age_c10 + year_c +
      susinidum_oh + susinidum_coc + susinidum_pbc + susinidum_mar +
      dg_psiq_cie_10_instudy + dg_psiq_cie_10_dg +
      prim_sub_daily + occ24_inactive + occ24_unemployed +
      susprindum_coc + susprindum_pbc + susprindum_mar
    
    # Freeze row universe
    mf0  <- stats::model.frame(ff_local, data = df, na.action = stats::na.pass)
    keep <- stats::complete.cases(mf0)
    mf   <- mf0[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(mf) == 0L) return(NULL)
    
    # Outcome variation check
    y <- stats::model.response(mf)
    if (length(unique(y)) < 2L) {
      return(tibble::tibble(
        plan_type_mod = as.character(.y),
        n_rows = nrow(mf),
        term = "(skipped: no outcome variation)",
        `RR (95% CI)` = NA_character_
      ))
    }
    
    # Design matrix
    X <- stats::model.matrix(ff_local, mf)
    assign_vec  <- attr(X, "assign")
    term_labels <- attr(stats::terms(ff_local), "term.labels")
    
    # Drop constants
    const <- vapply(as.data.frame(X),
                    function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1L,
                    logical(1))
    const[colnames(X) == "(Intercept)"] <- FALSE
    if (any(const)) {
      X <- X[, !const, drop = FALSE]
      assign_vec <- assign_vec[!const]
    }
    
    # Drop collinearity
    qrX <- qr(X)
    keep_cols <- sort(qrX$pivot[seq_len(qrX$rank)])
    assign_kept <- assign_vec[keep_cols]
    
    kept_term_idx <- sort(unique(assign_kept[assign_kept > 0]))
    if (length(kept_term_idx) == 0L) {
      return(tibble::tibble(
        plan_type_mod = as.character(.y),
        n_rows = nrow(mf),
        term = "(no predictors after cleanup)",
        `RR (95% CI)` = NA_character_
      ))
    }
    
    kept_terms <- term_labels[kept_term_idx]
    ff_reduced <- stats::reformulate(kept_terms,
                                     response = "tr_noncompletion")
    
    id_vec <- df$id[keep]
    
    fit <- geepack::geeglm(
      ff_reduced,
      id        = id_vec,
      data      = mf,
      family    = poisson,
      corstr    = "independence",
      scale.fix = TRUE,
      na.action = stats::na.exclude
    )
    
    broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        plan_type_mod = as.character(.y),
        n_rows        = nrow(mf),
        term,
        `RR (95% CI)` =
          sprintf("%.4f (%.4f, %.4f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
      )
  }) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::relocate(plan_type_mod, n_rows)
```

### Chunk 3: Run Stratified Models (Weighted Lag 0)

This chunk replicates the analysis using `w0_tr` weights.

```{r psu_count_w0}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

tab3_cnt_w0 <- 
  split(dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count,
        dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count$plan_type_mod) |>
  purrr::imap(~{
    df <- .x |> dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))
    
    ff_local <- tr_noncompletion ~ psu_ord +
      age_c10 + year_c +
      susinidum_oh + susinidum_coc + susinidum_pbc + susinidum_mar +
      dg_psiq_cie_10_instudy + dg_psiq_cie_10_dg +
      prim_sub_daily + occ24_inactive + occ24_unemployed +
      susprindum_coc + susprindum_pbc + susprindum_mar
    
    mf0  <- stats::model.frame(ff_local, data = df, na.action = stats::na.pass)
    keep <- stats::complete.cases(mf0)
    mf   <- mf0[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(mf) == 0L) return(NULL)
    
    y <- stats::model.response(mf)
    if (length(unique(y)) < 2L) {
      return(tibble::tibble(
        plan_type_mod = as.character(.y),
        n_rows = nrow(mf),
        term = "(skipped: no outcome variation)",
        `RR (95% CI)` = NA_character_
      ))
    }
    
    X <- stats::model.matrix(ff_local, mf)
    assign_vec  <- attr(X, "assign")
    term_labels <- attr(stats::terms(ff_local), "term.labels")
    
    const <- vapply(as.data.frame(X),
                    function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1L,
                    logical(1))
    const[colnames(X) == "(Intercept)"] <- FALSE
    if (any(const)) {
      X <- X[, !const, drop = FALSE]
      assign_vec <- assign_vec[!const]
    }
    
    qrX <- qr(X)
    keep_cols <- sort(qrX$pivot[seq_len(qrX$rank)])
    assign_kept <- assign_vec[keep_cols]
    
    kept_term_idx <- sort(unique(assign_kept[assign_kept > 0]))
    if (length(kept_term_idx) == 0L) return(NULL)
    
    kept_terms <- term_labels[kept_term_idx]
    ff_reduced <- stats::reformulate(kept_terms,
                                     response = "tr_noncompletion")
    
    id_vec <- df$id[keep]
    
    fit <- geepack::geeglm(
      ff_reduced,
      id        = id_vec,
      data      = mf,
      family    = poisson,
      corstr    = "independence",
      scale.fix = TRUE,
      na.action = stats::na.exclude,
      weights   = df$w0_tr[keep]
    )
    
    broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        plan_type_mod = as.character(.y),
        n_rows        = nrow(mf),
        term,
        `RR (95% CI)` =
          sprintf("%.4f (%.4f, %.4f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
      )
  }) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::relocate(plan_type_mod, n_rows)
```

### Chunk 4: Run Stratified Models (Weighted Lag 1)

This chunk runs the analysis using `w1_tr` weights and also calculates the counts for each ordinal PSU category (`n_rows_psu`) to include in the final table.

```{r psu_count_w1}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

tab3_cnt_w1 <- 
  split(dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count,
        dat_with_weights_stab_cons_count$plan_type_mod) |>
  purrr::imap(~{
    df <- .x |> dplyr::mutate(id = as.character(id))
    
    ff_local <- tr_noncompletion ~ psu_ord +
      age_c10 + year_c +
      susinidum_oh + susinidum_coc + susinidum_pbc + susinidum_mar +
      dg_psiq_cie_10_instudy + dg_psiq_cie_10_dg +
      prim_sub_daily + occ24_inactive + occ24_unemployed +
      susprindum_coc + susprindum_pbc + susprindum_mar
    
    mf0  <- stats::model.frame(ff_local, data = df, na.action = stats::na.pass)
    keep <- stats::complete.cases(mf0)
    mf   <- mf0[keep, , drop = FALSE]
    
    # Counts by ordinal PSU category in estimation sample
    n_psu_01 <- sum(mf$psu_ord == "0-1")
    n_psu_2  <- sum(mf$psu_ord == "2")
    n_psu_3p <- sum(mf$psu_ord == "3+")
    
    if (nrow(mf) == 0L) return(NULL)
    
    y <- stats::model.response(mf)
    if (length(unique(y)) < 2L) return(NULL)
    
    X <- stats::model.matrix(ff_local, mf)
    assign_vec  <- attr(X, "assign")
    term_labels <- attr(stats::terms(ff_local), "term.labels")
    
    const <- vapply(as.data.frame(X),
                    function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1L,
                    logical(1))
    const[colnames(X) == "(Intercept)"] <- FALSE
    if (any(const)) {
      X <- X[, !const, drop = FALSE]
      assign_vec <- assign_vec[!const]
    }
    
    qrX <- qr(X)
    keep_cols <- sort(qrX$pivot[seq_len(qrX$rank)])
    assign_kept <- assign_vec[keep_cols]
    
    kept_term_idx <- sort(unique(assign_kept[assign_kept > 0]))
    if (length(kept_term_idx) == 0L) return(NULL)
    
    kept_terms <- term_labels[kept_term_idx]
    ff_reduced <- stats::reformulate(kept_terms,
                                     response = "tr_noncompletion")
    
    id_vec <- df$id[keep]
    
    fit <- geepack::geeglm(
      ff_reduced,
      id        = id_vec,
      data      = mf,
      family    = poisson,
      corstr    = "independence",
      scale.fix = TRUE,
      na.action = stats::na.exclude,
      weights   = df$w1_tr[keep]
    )
    
    broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        n_rows_psu = dplyr::case_when(
          term == "psu_ord2"  ~ n_psu_2,
          term == "psu_ord3+" ~ n_psu_3p,
          TRUE                ~ NA_real_
        )
      ) |>
      dplyr::transmute(
        plan_type_mod = as.character(.y),
        n_rows_total  = nrow(mf),
        n_rows_psu,
        term,
        `RR (95% CI)` =
          sprintf("%.4f (%.4f, %.4f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
      )
  }) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::relocate(plan_type_mod, n_rows_total, n_rows_psu)
```

### Chunk 5: Final Summary Table

This chunk merges the results from the three models (Unweighted, Lag 0, Lag 1) and formats them into a final table suitable for reporting.

```{r psu_count_summary}
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: "hold"

### summary -----------------------------------------------------------------

format_ci <- function(x) {
  m <- stringr::str_match(x, "([0-9.]+) \\(([^,]+), ([^)]+)\\)")
  if(all(is.na(m))) return(x)
  est <- as.numeric(m[,2])
  lo  <- as.numeric(m[,3])
  hi  <- as.numeric(m[,4])
  sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", est, lo, hi)
}

rr_tab <-
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    cbind.data.frame(
      w = "no weight",
      dplyr::filter(tab3_cnt, grepl("psu_ord", term))
    ),
    cbind.data.frame(
      w = "weight lag=0",
      dplyr::filter(tab3_cnt_w0, grepl("psu_ord", term))
    ),
    cbind.data.frame(
      w = "weight lag=1",
      dplyr::filter(tab3_cnt_w1, grepl("psu_ord", term))
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = w,
    values_from = `RR (95% CI)`
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    plan_type_mod, term, n_rows,
    `no weight`, `weight lag=0`, `weight lag=1`
  )

psu_denoms <-
  tab3_cnt_w1 |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("psu_ord", term)) |>
  dplyr::select(plan_type_mod, term, n_rows_psu) |>
  dplyr::distinct()

final_tab <-
  rr_tab |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    psu_denoms,
    by = c("plan_type_mod", "term")
  )

final_tab_clean <-
  final_tab |>
  dplyr::group_by(plan_type_mod, term) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_rows     = max(n_rows, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_rows_psu = max(n_rows_psu, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    `no weight`    = dplyr::coalesce(`no weight`[1], `no weight`[2]),
    `weight lag=0` = dplyr::coalesce(`weight lag=0`[1], `weight lag=0`[2]),
    `weight lag=1` = dplyr::coalesce(`weight lag=1`[1], `weight lag=1`[2]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

final_tab_clean_fmt <-
  final_tab_clean |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      c(`no weight`, `weight lag=0`, `weight lag=1`),
      format_ci
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  final_tab_clean_fmt,
  format  = "markdown",
  caption = "Stratified Poisson GEE models using number of substances reported at admission",
  digits  = 2
)
```
